analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1030-1047), a documentation paragraph describing a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge. The supplied units are BASE text for lines 1-796, which are unchanged by the patch, so the changed region is visible only in the patch excerpt. No executable code is supplied, so no control regressions can be verified.

Security-relevant claims in the doc:
- Token-ID reuse is partitioned by the prefix-cache scope, and "reuse never crosses a cache scope". This is consistent with the T-041 scoping model (coordinator-authored cacheSalt, cross-account isolation).
- The cache is in-process and keyed by text pieces. Nothing in the excerpt says it persists to disk, so it does not appear to touch the at-rest SSD tier or its HMAC-lookup guarantees.
- A same-scope timing oracle (SEC-035, accepted) could widen slightly. Per-scope piece reuse makes a TTFT difference possible for repeated text within one account/model scope. That is the same trust boundary as the accepted risk, so it is not a new cross-tenant exposure, provided the scope key is actually the authenticated cacheScope.
- The doc says sampled background comparisons disable reuse on mismatch, and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 restores the old path. Both are fail-safe.
- Parallel encoding (up to four cores) and the rewritten templates (ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) are performance changes. The correctness equivalence of the rewritten templates is asserted, not verified.

Open integration questions for any code pass:
- Is PromptTokenCache keyed strictly by the coordinator-authored cacheScope, with no fallback to a global scope when no scope is present?
- Is the cache memory-bounded (DoS)?
- Do the ChatTemplateLoopRewrites render identically for adversarial consumer-supplied message histories? A divergence would affect prompt integrity.
- Is the background comparison failure path safe?
No threat-model update is needed beyond possibly noting piece-level token caching under SEC-035. No findings.
